evidenceBoundary.exact: Complete selected pdata bodies, chained fragments, registered generic method identities and instruction windows.
evidenceBoundary.direct: Reviewed code/dataflow equivalence to the registered reference-sharing ReadValue<T> and ReadArray<T> bodies; only these exact targets are admitted.
evidenceBoundary.conditional: Reference-typed Param<T> and ParamOutput<T> carriers must independently prove their exact class base, matching reader MethodSpec, generic carrier, element kind and full type; setter/read order and owning consumer validation remain required. The reference-sharing body carries MethodInfo through the same provider/dispatch dataflow without specializing the child wire grammar. Hidden-output-16 facts require an independently proved matching 16-byte result ABI and MethodSpec; they never admit a reference-return caller. The ReadPackable fact is limited to the explicitly reviewed normal-reference/cache/ABI conditions; it proves no error-path observational parity. Hidden-output-40 requires its own proven output/reader/MethodInfo ABI and typed caller; no child grammar or provider selection follows.
evidenceBoundary.unresolved: No new Param wire schema, source-corpus admission or runtime gameplay effect is established.

proof.inputs: RCX reader is saved in RDI; RDX MethodInfo is saved in RBX. Initialize its RGCTX at +0x38, take RGCTX[0] as the formatter-provider MethodInfo, and initialize a null result local.
proof.inlinedProvider: The clone inlines the complete provider at 0x185003f90: both load provider RGCTX[0], obtain its runtime type key, use the identical cache and monitor cells, hash/probe/insert with the same callees, including chained fallback fragments, and obtain the same R14 cache entry. Both pass R14 through 0x185004510, resolve the identical expected formatter type from provider RGCTX, and use the same type check and exception path. RBP holds the provider MethodInfo in both. Clone stack locals differ by +0x18 and it reloads the saved reader after the cache loop.
proof.registeredBody: The registered ReadValue<System.Object> body independently initializes a null local, loads MethodInfo.RGCTX[0], calls that same provider, and invokes virtual slot 5 with formatter, reader and address of result. The clone performs exactly this invocation after the inlined provider and returns its result local.
proof.dispatch: Both pass ECX=5, RDX=formatter, R8=reader, R9=&null-initialized result to the same dispatch helper. Its generic path preserves all operands and invokes the slot with its MethodInfo; selected optimized branches are shared by both callers.
proof.boundary: This proves the reference-sharing generic read, not a special Param formatter layout.

proof.inputs: Clone and registered ReadValue<LangKey> receive RCX=16-byte output, RDX=reader, R8=the same declared MethodInfo. Both save these operands, initialize MethodInfo.RGCTX at +0x38 when needed, zero all 16 output bytes, initialize the same provider class and pass MethodInfo.RGCTX[0] to the same provider.
proof.classInitialization: The registered seven-instruction class-initialization helper tests class+0xe0 and calls the same initializer only at zero. The clone inlines that branch and preserves the saved operands.
proof.nullProvider: Both return the already zeroed output when the provider returns null. Otherwise the clone inlines the complete selected dispatch helper. Both initialize the formatter class, read its slot-5 function/MethodInfo at +0x190/+0x198, and compare with the identical GenericMemoryPackFormatter<T,Wrapper>.Deserialize body.
proof.genericPath: On the nonmatching slot, both forward formatter, reader, output and slot MethodInfo unchanged. The dispatcher restores its frame before a tail jump; the clone calls the same slot then restores its frame and returns the output pointer. Normal returning ABI calls and no caller-address observation are conditions.
proof.selectedFastPath: Both test/refill one byte with the same helpers and treat FF as null/zero output. Otherwise both obtain the same wrapper type/context, create/default the same wrapper reference, call the same provider and slot-5 helper with reader and the wrapper-reference local, then resolve the same conversion interface by the same slot scan/fallback and invoke it with a 16-byte hidden-output local.
proof.locals: Clone output/reader are RSI/RDI; dispatcher output/reader are RDI/RSI until their last reads. Wrapper locals are clone stack+0x50 versus dispatcher stack+0x68; conversion output is stack+0x20 in both. The clone pre-saves R14/RBP, whereas the dispatcher saves R14 only on the path using it; all returning paths restore the same incoming nonvolatile state. Local addresses may be renamed only under ordinary nonescaping, address-independent formatter/converter behavior.
proof.outputAndBarrier: Null converted wrappers zero all 16 output bytes. Nonnull conversion results copy exactly 16 bytes from returned RAX to the same incoming output pointer. Both test the same GC flag and set the same bitmap bit from output>>12, with identical mask, bitmap cell, BTS and locked CMPXCHG loop. The clone uses R8 to preserve its output register; the dispatcher restores its original output register before returning to the registered caller, which returns that pointer.
proof.scope: Whole selected original bodies and complete branch/loop paths were reviewed. This is a hidden-output LangKey read equivalence under the stated ABI, stable valid storage and ordinary helper/formatter conditions. It does not prove a caller setup, owning serialized schema, full NPC decode, live generic binding, runtime patches or gameplay effects.

proof.inputs: Registered ReadPackable<Object> preserves RCX reader, initializes incoming RDX MethodInfo, loads RGCTX[0] and tail-jumps to the already reviewed reference ReadValue. Its selected static slot is ReadValue<the reciprocal ordinal-zero MVAR of ReadPackable>. The optimized clone performs both nested context loads and their initialization before reading provider RGCTX[0]. RBP then holds the same GetFormatter<T> MethodInfo; it is saved across cache code.
proof.typeAPI: The named current Type.GetTypeFromHandle program and the clone derive the same native handle through the same class/type helper, then use exactly the same native type-cache cell, RuntimeType allocation cell, eight-byte value array, 24-byte hash entries, hash/equality/trait callees and monitor cells. The initial shared lookup and exclusive recheck return the selected existing value; the miss constructs the same RuntimeType with its handle at +0x10. Registers and nonescaping locals are renamed only under ordinary ABI and coherent synchronized-cache conditions.
proof.growthCopy: The canonical value-array growth calls the checked 21-instruction hook wrapper with the checked eight-instruction copy callback. The clone expands those same two hook-cell reads/calls and the identical memcpy arguments. Current helper grammars check this expansion. The callback return and outgoing flags are dead at both owner callsites. New capacity, source size, release call, barrier and array/capacity stores agree.
proof.insertion: The clone expands the complete current 222-instruction insertion helper with the canonical argument tuple {word=0,key=native handle,valueIndex=count-minus-deleted}. Its cache owner is RDI instead of helper RBX; probe index RSI replaces helper RDI, first available slot R14 replaces helper R15, and the unchanged key/value-index live in frame locals. The empty-word comparisons specialize the supplied zero word. Both use the same probe/mask, trait, count, resize, floating load-factor, rehash, disposal, overflow and key/word/value-index stores. Coherent finite cache state, stable internal equality and normal synchronized helper effects are required; ignored iterator/status results do not reach the read result.
proof.provider: Each successful cache path reloads the original reader from its saved incoming home and restores the saved provider MethodInfo. The clone calls a fully inventoried provider wrapper that forwards the exact Type reference to the same provider core as the reviewed ReadValue, adding only matching metadata/provider-class initialization. Both obtain expected MemoryPackFormatter<T> from provider RGCTX[1] and use the same assignability helper. Concrete live provider/formatter selection remains a condition, not an observation.
proof.result: The clone initializes its complete eight-byte output local to zero. On the compatible nonnull formatter path, ECX=5, RDX=formatter, R8=the original reader and R9=that local reach the identical dispatch helper used by the registered ReadValue. The sole ordinary RET reloads exactly that local into RAX and restores all saved nonvolatile registers and the original frame. The three encoded-metadata tables belong to the separately inventoried formatter-error construction path, not to a different normal read.
proof.scope: Normal reference-sharing read equivalence only: valid disjoint storage, matching initialized MethodInfo/RGCTX, coherent synchronized native type cache and provider registry, finite valid probes, and successful normal ABI-preserving runtime/cache/allocator/monitor/GC-hook calls with address-independent behavior. Caller return-address, temporary-address and profiler observations, error/exception-message/stack parity, invalid metadata/cache states, concrete live formatter choice, child wire grammar, owning schema and execution are not proved.
